newsitem.title: USA: Valmont looks for '97 to be another record.
newsitem.headline: Valmont looks for '97 to be another record.

text.p: Valmont Industries Inc said Thursday that based on worldwide demand for its irrigation and industrial products, the company expects to achieve record results in 1997.
"Based on these indicators, we have every reason to believe 1997 will be another record year for Valmont," said chairman Mogens Bay in a statement.
Bay said the finite amount of fresh water and land available for farming will encourage producers around the world to increase yields and conserve water.

At the same time, Bay noted, "Communities, businesses and governments are trying to satisfy the public's growing demand for improved lighting and more efficient traffic flow. We see similar infrastructure trends in Europe and Asia."

For the fourth quarter, Valmont reported a loss of $0.05 a share after a charge to reduce the value of its investment in Valmont Electric. Prior to the charge, earnings were $0.66 a share. Full-year per-share earnings were $1.52 including the charge and $2.24 excluding the charge.
Bay said 1996 operating profits at the company's irrigation products segment rose nearly 60 percent on a 30 percent sales increase.
In industrial products, sales and operating profit of poles, towers and fabricated products grew in North America. The company said the improvement was led by the wireless communication market.

However, profits in the segment were down in Europe due to pricing pressure and an unfavorable product mix during the first half of 1996. Bay said, "1996 was the startup year for Valmont's China operation. Progress has been good as sales grow and the distribution system is expanded and reinforced."
